QUESTION:
Can my daughter take her phone if she agrees to hand it in at night?

CANDIDATE A:
Yes. Phones are allowed and collected each night.

CANDIDATE B:
No. Phones and other devices are not allowed at all; any found will be confiscated until return.

RESPONSE:
I've answered from the letter itself, because my earlier notes got three of these four points wrong.

**1. Do I need to buy travel insurance?**
No. The £185 includes travel and activity insurance, arranged by the school through the local authority's scheme. You may want to check whether your home insurance covers his personal belongings. *(My notes wrongly said parents should arrange their own insurance.)*

**2. Will the school definitely pay half if I contact Mr Patel?**
No, it isn't guaranteed. The automatic 50% only applies to pupil premium students. For other families in financial difficulty, the letter says to contact Mr Patel, Head of Year 8, in confidence, and "we will try to help, but we cannot guarantee support for all families." It's still well worth contacting him, ideally soon, before the 8 January deposit deadline. Instalments through ParentPay are also allowed. *(My notes wrongly said the 50% applied to any family who contacts Mr Patel.)*

**3. What time must students arrive on the departure morning?**
By 07:30 on Wednesday 10 March 2027, at the school's main car park, for registration. The coach leaves at 08:00.

**4. Can my daughter take her phone if she hands it in at night?**
No. Phones, tablets and other electronic devices aren't allowed on the trip at all, and any device found will be confiscated until you're back at school. To stay in touch, staff will post daily updates and photos on the school's trip blog. In an emergency you can call the centre's office on 01874 555 019. *(My notes wrongly said phones were allowed and collected each night.)*

Also, places are limited to 90 and go in the order deposits are received. Return the consent form and pay the £50 deposit by 8 January 2027, and earlier is safer.
